title: Make secondary mailbox wake race-safe
description: Send both a targeted IPI and SEV for every SMP mailbox publication and acknowledge the physical IPI unconditionally before running the callback.
reason: A secondary CPU could cross the global WFI-to-WFE transition while the sender selected only one wake mechanism.
problem_fixed: Windows secondary startup reset or hung immediately after the CPU1 mailbox was published.
reproduction: Boot the pre-fix eight-core image and observe that the log stops after 'Secondary 1 published' without the matching consume or guest-entry marker.
implementation: Changed the m1n1 SMP mailbox notification protocol only; no timer, vGIC, Mu, NVMe, display, input, or Windows change.
verification: Nested SMP Python suite 10/10 and complete nested C host suite passed.
hardware_result: All seven secondary mailboxes were consumed exactly once; CPUs 0 through 7 emitted CPU_ENTRY and remained live through the passive observation window.
notes: Do not infer guest death from the persistent proxy USB endpoint or launcher exit.

title: Record canonical J313 stability checkpoint
description: Pinned the hardware-tested EXP016 artifacts and documented the valid passive-observation contract.
reason: Earlier results mixed runtimes and a competing proxy observer caused an EL2 abort that was incorrectly attributable to the guest.
problem_fixed: Ambiguous assisted-boot results and unsafe use of a second proxy owner against a live guest.
reproduction: Launch a guest and attach hang_telemetry.py as a second proxy client; the old path reports an unhandled callback and can reset EL2.
implementation: Recorded exact m1n1 and Mu hashes; made direct telemetry attach fail closed; retained one proxy owner and passive log observation.
verification: Root Python suite 242/242 passed; EXP016 clean rerun remained alive for more than three minutes with no bugcheck, watchdog, exception, panic, or reset marker.
hardware_result: Canonical eight-core launch passed preflight and CPU_ENTRY for CPUs 0 through 7; operator desktop responsiveness remained explicitly unclaimed.
notes: Never attach a standalone observer while the assisted launcher owns asynchronous proxy callbacks.

title: Add machine-readable change ledger
description: Added an RFC 4180 CSV index and an automated schema test for every feature, correction, and workflow change.
reason: Long narrative documents made it difficult to find the exact commit, motivation, reproduction, verification, artifact, and hardware result for a past change.
problem_fixed: Repeated investigation or accidental reuse of a rejected approach because the evidence was scattered across prose and chat history.
reproduction: Remove investigation/CHANGES.csv or a required field and run './proxyenv/bin/python -m unittest tests.test_change_ledger -v'; the schema contract fails.
implementation: Defined required columns and statuses in tests; added the mandatory two-commit bookkeeping workflow to AGENTS.md; seeded the ledger with the canonical SMP and stability checkpoints.
verification: Observed the focused test fail before the CSV existed; after implementation the focused suite passed 2/2 and the complete project suite passed 244/244 in proxyenv.
notes: A ledger-only bookkeeping commit does not require its own recursive row.

title: Reduce secondary recovery polling to 100 Hz
description: Restored the non-ECV secondary EL2 heartbeat from 1000 Hz to 100 Hz while retaining the race-safe SMP mailbox and vGIC progress path.
reason: EXP017 was materially slower and showed continuous pointer micro-stutter; the extra seven thousand EL2 entries per second were the only continuous-rate CPU-policy difference from the earlier responsive baseline.
problem_fixed: This change improved initial responsiveness but did not fix the underlying timer-progress loss and therefore is rejected.
reproduction: Boot EXP017 and observe slow startup and continuous pointer micro-stutter; boot EXP018 and wait for an intermittent minute-scale global stall.
implementation: Changed only HV_FALLBACK_SECONDARY_TICK_RATE from 1000 to 100 and updated its policy test.
verification: RED tick-policy test failed at 1000; complete nested C host suite and focused SMP Python suite 10/10 passed after the change.
hardware_result: All eight CPUs entered Windows and responsiveness initially improved; Windows then stopped responding for at least one minute and later recovered without reboot. Two snapshots showed advancing hardware counters plus Pending-only 0x502 and Active-only 0x902 INTID 18 LRs. Diagnostic IPIs briefly kicked timer IAR/EOI activity, so spontaneous versus wake-assisted recovery remains unresolved.
notes: Do not tune the polling frequency again; repair event-driven guest timer/vGIC progress.

title: Preserve level-sensitive guest timer delivery
description: Made the sampled Apple timer line and live LR state authoritative; Active reassertion becomes Active+Pending, deassertion withdraws Pending, and deferred INTID 17/18 ownership is unique and withdrawable.
reason: EXP018 proved that lowering recovery polling removed continuous overhead but exposed minute-scale stalls with Pending-only and Active-only timer LRs while physical counters advanced.
problem_fixed: The boolean-first timer path skipped re-pending whenever its latch was true, so a timer reasserted during Active could be lost until a later physical wake or recovery tick.
reproduction: Boot EXP018, wait for the minute-scale global pause, and inspect snapshots showing asserted timers without an Active+Pending transition.
implementation: Added a pure LR level state machine, a fixed per-CPU two-source deferred owner, one production synchronizer for INTIDs 17 and 18, stale-Pending withdrawal, EOI/maintenance timer drain before VI recomputation, and no redundant post-injection LR rescan.
verification: Observed three RED stages; mutation test caught Active-to-Active-only; complete nested C suite, SMP Python 10/10, root Python 247/247, diff checks and clean post-commit freestanding build passed.
notes: Hardware result will be appended after the recorded assisted EXP019 run; heartbeat remains 100 Hz.

title: Expose monitor and foreground modes through the canonical launcher
description: Allowed run-windows.sh to select the already-supported assisted debug=monitor profile and keep the runner in the foreground when requested.
reason: EXP019 requires passive UART capture without framebuffer streaming or forensic telemetry through the sole public entrypoint, and the runner must outlive a short command session.
problem_fixed: The lower run-assisted.sh accepted monitor and foreground operation, but run-windows.sh rejected monitor and could only dispatch detached children; the first hardware attempt lost both host processes before Windows acceptance.
reproduction: Run scripts/run-windows.sh --execution assisted --display physical --debug monitor --foreground --dry-run before this commit; monitor exits 2 and foreground is unavailable.
implementation: Extended usage validation, artifact mapping and forwarding for monitor/foreground while preserving the existing lower launcher contract.
verification: The monitor test failed with exit 2 and the lifecycle test lacked foreground before the change; both passed afterward and exact EXP019 dry-run resolved physical display, monitor UART, foreground runner, no USB framebuffer, no telemetry, and the recorded public m1n1 path.
notes: Host-lifecycle correction discovered by preflight/attempt 1; it does not change guest binaries.

title: Measure host recovery timer progress
description: Added per-CPU host CNTP arm, recovery-arm and expiry counters plus host timer control/comparator fields to watchdog snapshots.
reason: Existing snapshots exposed the guest timer view only and could not distinguish a missing EL2 wake from a delivery failure after the wake.
problem_fixed: Ambiguous timer stalls where a Pending LR persisted but it was unknown whether the 1-ms recovery source actually fired.
reproduction: Boot EXP025 and compare two snapshots while Windows is slow; guest IAR/EOI barely changes and no host recovery expiry evidence exists.
implementation: Instrumented the host CNTP path without intentionally changing scheduling or timer policy.
verification: Focused source contract, complete nested host suite, root vGIC suite, diff check and post-commit build passed.
hardware_result: EXP026 proved host recovery arms and fires near 1 kHz on several vCPUs while Windows remains slow; the diagnostic succeeded and the build is rejected as a performance fix.
notes: The operator later reported INTERNAL_POWER_ERROR; exact parameters were not captured in EXP026.

title: Keep completed local virtual IRQ delivery off the global lock
description: Allows an eligible secondary FIQ to return directly after local timer/IPI service and live-LR HCR.VI recomputation even when a virtual IRQ is Pending.
reason: EXP026 measured nearly continuous recovery FIQs and showed that each Pending virtual timer forced the legacy globally serialized bhl path, which can starve Windows scheduling and runtime-power workers.
problem_fixed: Slow boot, long global stalls, CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT and a reported INTERNAL_POWER_ERROR consistent with blocked runtime-power work.
reproduction: Boot EXP026; observe recovery arm/fire counters growing near 1 kHz on several CPUs while every virtual-pending secondary enters the slow global-lock path.
implementation: Removed virtual-pending state from the local completion predicate; physical FIQs, rendezvous, proxy switches and the interruptible CPU remain serialized, while the recovery wake remains active until acknowledgement.
verification: The focused policy test failed before implementation and passed afterward; complete nested host suite, root vGIC contract suite, diff check and post-commit freestanding build passed.
notes: Hardware result pending; ESP unchanged and Mu is identical to EXP026.

title: Restore accepted timer delivery path
description: Removed the experimental 1 ms recovery source and restored the accepted timer latch and repend behavior while retaining the race-safe SMP wake.
reason: The recovery source generated excessive EL2 work and changed timer behavior beyond the accepted baseline.
problem_fixed: The experimental recovery build was slow and ended in a 0x133 watchdog; the restored path still produced long intermittent freezes.
reproduction: Boot EXP028 and observe recovery activity and 0x133; boot EXP029 with recovery disabled and wait through lock-screen activity.
implementation: Returned timer delivery to the accepted pre-recovery implementation without changing Mu, NVMe, xHCI, CPU count, or SMP wake.
verification: Nested host suite, root vGIC contracts, SMP tests and freestanding build passed.
hardware_result: Windows reached the lock screen but froze repeatedly; snapshots showed live CPUs and empty queues, and diagnostic wake requests temporarily restored progress.
notes: Restoring the accepted timer path removed one regression but did not remove the underlying idle-wake stall.

title: Restore accepted CPU0 service cadence
description: Restored the boot CPU service tick to the accepted fixed 5000 Hz while keeping secondary CPUs at 100 Hz.
reason: The post-baseline tree had reduced CPU0 first to 1000 Hz and then 100 Hz, which changed the only always-on service cadence used by the previously responsive build.
problem_fixed: EXP029 froze intermittently with CPU0 below the accepted cadence; EXP030 restores the exact 5000/100 split.
reproduction: Boot EXP030 and verify the 5000-to-5000 runtime marker, all eight CPU entries, then observe lock-screen and SSH continuity.
implementation: Changed only hv_boot_tick_rate and hv_runtime_tick_rate for CPU0 to 5000 Hz.
verification: RED tick policy test failed at 1000 Hz; complete nested host suite, root vGIC suite, SMP suite and freestanding build passed.
hardware_result: All CPUs, NVMe and xHCI initialized and Windows accepted SSH, but intermittent pauses still stopped sessions and later recovered.
notes: The cadence correction improves fidelity to the baseline but monitor overhead remains a confounding variable.

title: Make release snapshots zero-cost
description: Return from the watchdog snapshot tick before sampling when runtime diagnostics are disabled.
reason: At the restored 5000 Hz CPU0 cadence the monitor sampler performed architectural and LR-bank reads about 78 times per second even for production-oriented runs.
problem_fixed: Release-profile overhead and UI pauses may be amplified by a monitor-only sampler that still executes in the hot path.
reproduction: Run the release source-contract test before the guard and observe failure; build EXP031 with RELEASE=1 and compare physical UI and SSH continuity with EXP030.
implementation: Added one early runtime-diagnostics guard without changing timer delivery, CPU cadence, Mu, storage, USB, display, or Windows.
verification: RED source-contract test failed before the guard; root vGIC suite 16/16, focused release/watchdog/fast-path/tick tests, complete nested host suite and clean RELEASE build passed.
notes: Hardware A/B pending; Apple Input is disabled and diagnostics are off.

title: Require both displays for observed investigations
description: Added an explicit observed assisted-launch mode that selects display=both, starts the framebuffer viewer and rejects an explicit non-both display.
reason: Physical-only tests leave the entire Windows-logo-to-network interval invisible and previously allowed a slow boot, guest freeze, DCP failure and network delay to be confused.
problem_fixed: Problem investigations could continue without knowing whether the Windows framebuffer was progressing.
reproduction: Run the pre-change public launcher with --observed and see usage failure; or run a physical-only investigation and lose independent framebuffer evidence before SSH.
implementation: Added the observed flag and a fail-closed display contract while preserving the quiet physical-only final performance profile.
verification: RED observed-profile test failed with usage exit 2; focused GREEN passed and complete public launcher suite passed 34/34.
notes: Use observed mode for every unknown, regression or freeze; physical-only is reserved for final performance acceptance.

title: Keep framebuffer events below 4 KiB
description: Reduced the framebuffer payload so a complete proxy event is 4072 bytes instead of 16360 bytes.
reason: EXP032 recorded corruption only on maximum type-3 framebuffer events at the 16-KiB DWC3 boundary; the shared CDC stream then emitted NUL runs and the web viewer stopped before the physical display.
problem_fixed: The mandatory display=both observer lost USB framing and could not distinguish the later Windows freeze from transport failure.
reproduction: Boot EXP032 and observe viewer generation 31 stop at the Windows logo while the physical panel reaches lock screen; the proxy reports type=3 length=16348 with a zero wire checksum.
implementation: Changed only HV_FB_STREAM_PAYLOAD_SIZE from 0x3fc0 to 0x0fc0 and added a literal complete-event safe-budget regression assertion.
verification: RED USB-limit test aborted at 16360 bytes; GREEN focused tests passed; complete nested host suite passed; root display and launcher suite passed 54/54.
hardware_result: EXP033 advanced from generation 16/frame 15 to generation 75/frame 74 with valid checksums and no framing loss while the unchanged guest framebuffer froze at the Windows boot logo.
notes: Observer transport is hardware-validated; the reproduced guest freeze remains a separate unresolved runtime defect.

title: Remove release tick diagnostic writes
description: Made diagnostic counter increments compile-time no-ops in RELEASE while retaining them in debug builds.
reason: Commit 89d41fac added an atomic shared-array update to every host timer arm and another counter write to every expired host tick even though release snapshots return before consuming them.
problem_fixed: The 5000-Hz CPU0 EL2 path and seven 100-Hz secondary paths performed useless diagnostic cache writes that were absent from the last responsive baseline and could stall coherent progress.
reproduction: Boot EXP033 and observe the valid framebuffer freeze at the Windows logo; disassemble its release hv_arm_tick and observe the diagnostic counter RMW introduced after the baseline.
implementation: Added one runtime-diagnostic counter contract and routed the two arm counters plus host_tick_fires through it; timer registers and delivery policy are unchanged.
verification: RED host compilation failed on the missing contract; GREEN debug/release behavior passed; full nested host suite passed; release hv_arm_tick disassembly has no counter RMW/store and retains CNTP_TVAL/CNTP_CTL writes.
hardware_result: The exact EXP035 artifact reproduced the frozen Windows-logo framebuffer for over two minutes with valid advancing observer generations and no TCP/22; an external diagnostic wake then immediately advanced guest initialization.
notes: Retain the zero-cost release cleanup, but do not attribute the freeze to diagnostic writes; investigate the lost virtual-IRQ wake boundary.

title: Resynchronize virtual IRQ before secondary return
description: Recomputes synthetic HCR.VI once from final local LR and VMCR state after secondary timer and IPI service and before the abbreviated return decision.
reason: EXP029 and EXP035 showed that a diagnostic EL2 wake immediately restored guest progress; commit 2ae94af removed the fast-boundary recomputation retained by the last desktop-reaching checkpoint.
problem_fixed: A timer LR can remain Pending while the accepted delivery latch skips fresh inject and repend helpers; if HCR.VI was cleared by an intervening vGIC transition the secondary returns to Windows idle with no guaranteed physical wake.
reproduction: Boot EXP035 and wait for the byte-identical Windows-logo freeze; request an external diagnostic boundary and observe immediate progress to guest-runtime and xHCI route checkpoints.
implementation: Added exactly one hv_vgic3_update_vi call after local timer and IPI handling and before reading HCR.VI; no timer rate recovery source or global exception scan changed.
verification: Focused test failed at zero recomputations before implementation; focused and vGIC 16/16 passed after; nested C host suite and complete root suite 255/255 passed.
hardware_result: EXP036 advanced autonomously beyond EXP035 to the lock screen, proving an early lost-wake correction, but then froze on one byte-identical frame for over two minutes with no TCP/22; a diagnostic boundary did not restore it.
notes: Keep the partial wake correction, but a later timer or idle-wake failure remains; capture a monitor snapshot at that checkpoint before another policy change.

title: Preserve LR bank in watchdog dump
description: Formats the existing watchdog summary and LR bank in two bounded calls while retaining one newline-delimited logical CPU record.
reason: EXP037's monitor snapshots truncated exactly after the marker field because one formatted record exceeded the console buffer; all LR state needed to distinguish Pending from Active delivery was lost.
problem_fixed: Timer stalls could not be classified safely and a delivery-policy change would have guessed whether vinj referred to a Pending Active Active+Pending or absent LR.
reproduction: Run EXP037 and inspect hv.log: each HV WATCHDOG CPU record ends at marker and contains no lrc or lr0 fields.
implementation: Split only explicit snapshot formatting after marker; the second call appends lrc and eight LRs plus the original newline; sampled content and runtime code are unchanged.
verification: Focused source test failed before the split and passed after; vGIC and platform-stability suites passed 35/35 and the complete nested C host suite passed.
notes: Exact clean monitor artifact and strict manifest recorded before hardware use; hardware validation pending and this is not yet a guest stability fix.

title: Synchronize the live virtual timer level
description: Reflects the asserted and deasserted CNTV level into an already-live INTID 18 LR without changing INTID 17 queues tick cadence recovery or exit policy.
reason: EXP038 captured repeated Active-only INTID 18 LRs on CPUs 0 3 and 5 while CNTV_CTL=0x5 and vinj=1; Windows remained frozen until external EL2 boundaries.
problem_fixed: The accepted delivery latch treated any live LR as sufficient ownership so an expired level-sensitive timer acknowledged as Active never became Active+Pending and EOI exposed no next Pending tick.
reproduction: Boot EXP038 and wait at the disk-check or black-screen stall; decode two watchdog LR banks and observe 0x9020020000000012 with CNTV_CTL=0x5 on the same CPUs.
implementation: Added a change-only live-LR synchronizer around the existing tested four-state helper; the asserted virtual-timer latch maps Active to Active+Pending and deassertion maps Active+Pending to Active.
verification: RED production-path test failed on 3aeef41; GREEN focused tests passed 20/20 complete nested C host suite passed complete root suite passed 257/257 and diff checks passed.
hardware_result: EXP039 booted all eight CPUs and reached NVMe and xHCI runtime but froze on the disk-check countdown; observer generations advanced while the framebuffer remained byte-identical for more than two minutes and TCP/22 stayed absent; Stage 1 recovery succeeded.
notes: Hardware rejects sufficiency of live-LR level synchronization; preserve the architectural correction while investigating EOI deactivation and physical wake.

title: Wake deliverable timer VI on a physical edge
description: Issues one local physical self-IPI after publishing HCR.VI only on the false-to-true edge of a priority-deliverable Pending INTID 17 or 18.
reason: EXP040 proved that LR state and HCR.VI remain correct while Apple cores stay in the Windows idle path; each external physical IPI caused fresh timer IAR and EOI activity and guest progress.
problem_fixed: A synthetic VI transition alone does not reliably wake a J313 core from the guest WFI path so a correctly pending Windows architectural timer can remain unconsumed indefinitely.
reproduction: Boot EXP040 and capture byte-identical frames with Pending INTID 18 and HCR.VI asserted; request one diagnostic physical IPI and observe timer acknowledgement and framebuffer progress.
implementation: Scans deliverable Pending LRs for architectural timer INTIDs; after setting HCR.VI performs ISB then sends one local IPI only when the previous VI value was clear; Active+Pending and repeated asserted VI states do not kick.
verification: The helper test first failed to compile and the integration contract failed before production code; afterward focused 49/49 complete nested host tests and complete root 258/258 passed with clean diff checks.
hardware_result: EXP041 reached runtime but froze at the disk-check countdown; physical IPI receive counts then grew by about 18000 per CPU with no virtual IAR/EOI progress because the fast FIQ path acknowledged each self-IPI before guest ERET.
notes: The timer-edge classification is retained as evidence but immediate emission is superseded; defer any physical kick until the final EL2-to-guest return boundary.

title: Defer timer wake until guest return
description: Latches the existing deliverable timer VI edge and emits its local physical IPI only after the final local-source drain and hv_exc_exit on the FIQ path.
reason: EXP041 showed that immediate self-IPI delivery was acknowledged by hv_handle_local_ipi in the same EL2 exception before ERET; physical IPI counts grew while Windows virtual IAR/EOI remained frozen.
problem_fixed: The intended physical wake never remained pending at the EL2-to-guest boundary so it could not wake the guest after ERET.
reproduction: Boot EXP041 at the disk-check freeze and compare two snapshots; observe approximately 18000 new physical IPIs per active CPU with unchanged virtual IAR/EOI counters.
implementation: Replaced the immediate send with a cacheline-separated per-CPU deferred flag; the final FIQ path flushes it after hv_exc_exit and performs ISB before the local IPI.
verification: The ordering contract failed on the missing flush before implementation; afterward vGIC/platform suites passed 37/37 complete nested host tests passed and complete root tests passed 258/258 with clean diff checks.
hardware_result: EXP042 advanced one disk-check phase but froze again; CPU1 and CPU5 each received over 25000 deferred physical IPIs while virtual IAR/EOI remained unchanged because the HCR-derived edge repeatedly re-armed for the same Pending timer.
notes: Deferred placement is correct and retained; replace only HCR-bit edge identity with one latch per continuous deliverable Pending timer interval.

title: Latch one wake per deliverable Pending timer interval
description: Tracks per-CPU timer deliverability independently of HCR.VI and defers exactly one physical wake when a Pending INTID 17 or 18 first becomes priority-deliverable; the latch resets when that condition ends.
reason: EXP042 proved deferred placement but measured more than 25000 physical IPIs with unchanged virtual IAR/EOI because HCR.VI transitions do not identify one timer delivery lifecycle.
problem_fixed: Repeated physical FIQs for the same unconsumed Pending timer can starve the guest and recreate the apparent freeze the wake was intended to resolve.
reproduction: Boot EXP042 and compare snapshots around the static disk-check frame; CPU1 IPI rises 22065 to 48374 while IAR/EOI stays 14516 and CPU5 rises 19961 to 45404 while IAR/EOI stays 9286.
implementation: Added a tested two-state deliverability transition and cacheline-separated per-CPU latch; continuous deliverability suppresses repeat wakes and masking IAR or removal resets the interval while preserving the deferred FIQ-return send.
verification: The host state-transition test and root source contract failed before implementation; afterward vGIC/platform suites passed 37/37 complete nested host tests passed complete root tests passed 258/258 and diff checks passed.
hardware_result: EXP043 autonomously passed both former freeze frames and eliminated the repeated physical IPI storm but Windows later bugchecked with 0x133 P1=1 for cumulative time at IRQL DISPATCH_LEVEL or above; the final snapshot had no pending timer LR on CPUs 1 through 7.
notes: Do not retain as a stable fix or make a fourth incremental wake patch; collect the new Windows dump and perform an architectural A/B against the accepted 2026-08-13 contract.

title: Make trapped idle timer delivery deterministic
description: Makes HCR TWI and TWE plus the WFI/WFE exception path unconditional; keeps the proven live CNTV level-to-LR synchronization and removes the entire experimental physical timer self-IPI path.
reason: EXP044 measured frozen cores sleeping without TWI/TWE; EXP045 proved trapping alone reaches EL2 but leaves asserted Active timer LRs stale; EXP040 proved the complementary Active-to-Active+Pending level correction; EXP041 through EXP043 rejected physical self-IPIs.
problem_fixed: An idle Windows vCPU could sleep past a deliverable virtual timer or receive disruptive physical self-IPIs while the hypervisor failed to preserve the architectural level state in its live LR.
reproduction: Boot EXP044 to reproduce missing HCR bits and Active-only expired timers; boot EXP045 to reproduce the same stale LR with traps enabled; boot EXP043 to reproduce the 0x133 P1=1 self-IPI outcome.
implementation: Applies and verifies TWI/TWE on initial guarded HCR preflight secondary restore and every runtime whole-HCR write; handles trapped WFI/WFE in all profiles; removes timer wake latch deferred flush and physical self-IPI emission while retaining CNTV asserted/deasserted live-LR synchronization.
verification: RED source contracts failed on the optional flag and self-IPI path; focused timer WFX and vGIC tests passed; complete nested host suite passed; complete root suite passed 258/258; clean APPLE_INPUT=0 freestanding build passed; diff checks passed.
hardware_result: EXP046 reached all eight CPUs plus NVMe and xHCI but published the same black frame for more than two minutes; two snapshots 30 seconds apart had Pending INTID 18 and HCR.VI while every virtual IAR and EOI counter stayed unchanged; Stage 1 recovery succeeded.
notes: Static WFI/WFE trapping plus live level synchronization is insufficient and must not be promoted; test a dynamic trap coupled only to deliverable HCR.VI.

title: Trap idle only for a pending virtual IRQ
description: Couples HCR TWI and TWE exactly to HCR.VI so ordinary guest WFI/WFE retains architectural sleep while a vCPU cannot sleep again after a virtual interrupt becomes deliverable.
reason: EXP046 proved that permanently trapping idle creates a tight return regime with Pending timer LRs and unchanged virtual IAR/EOI; EXP040 proved a physical boundary can wake ordinary WFI and the existing host timer already provides that boundary.
problem_fixed: The static trap distorted every idle cycle while the no-trap path could return an awakened vCPU to sleep despite a newly published VI.
reproduction: Boot EXP046 and compare two snapshots more than 30 seconds apart; observe Pending INTID 18 plus HCR.VI and invariant IAR/EOI on all affected vCPUs while host ticks continue.
implementation: The whole-HCR policy helper now sets TWI/TWE only when the same value contains VI and clears them otherwise; initial and secondary HCR preserve normal idle; the existing WFI/WFE handler remains available only for the pending-VI window; no IPI timer LR or cadence behavior changed.
verification: RED helper and root source contracts failed before implementation; focused WFX timer and vGIC tests passed; complete nested host suite passed; complete root suite passed 258/258; clean APPLE_INPUT=0 freestanding build passed; diff checks passed.
hardware_result: All eight vCPUs plus NVMe and xHCI reached runtime, but two snapshots over 30 seconds apart showed Pending deliverable INTID 18 with VI plus TWI/TWE and unchanged virtual IAR/EOI; the framebuffer remained black and TCP/22 never appeared.
notes: Dynamic trapping obeys its contract but cannot wake an already sleeping Apple core; restore the separately validated one-shot physical doorbell and diagnose the later 0x133 independently.

title: Restore one deferred timer doorbell per deliverable interval
description: Reintroduced the EXP043 per-vCPU Pending timer latch and emitted a deferred local physical self-IPI after the final FIQ exit boundary.
reason: EXP047 proved a Pending deliverable virtual timer plus dynamic WFI trapping could not wake a core already sleeping on J313.
problem_fixed: A virtual VI transition alone lacks a reliable physical wake edge on the Apple idle path.
reproduction: Boot EXP047 and compare two snapshots showing Pending INTID18 with invariant IAR and EOI until an external physical boundary.
implementation: Added a cacheline-separated timer interval latch deferred flag and post-exit self-IPI flush without changing timer rates or LR priority.
verification: RED pure helper and integration contracts failed first; focused and complete nested suites passed; complete public suite passed 258/258; strict artifact preflight passed.
hardware_result: EXP048 passed the prior black frame and reached lock screen, but two snapshots measured hundreds of thousands of excess physical IPIs and the guest remained intermittently frozen; Stage1 recovered.
notes: The wake is effective but architecturally too expensive; remove the self-IPI mechanism and virtualize guest idle with a real EL2 wait.

title: Emulate trapped guest idle with a real EL2 wait
description: Replaced the rejected timer self-IPI state machine with unconditional WFI and WFE traps that wait in the lock-free EL2 synchronous path and skip the wait when HCR.VI is already asserted.
reason: EXP048 proved that a synthetic physical timer doorbell wakes Windows but creates hundreds of excess physical exceptions per second and reproduces micro-freezes.
problem_fixed: The timer wake mechanism itself overloaded the physical exception path while the guest still required an architectural idle boundary.
reproduction: Boot EXP048 and compare physical IPI receive growth with ordinary virtual-SGI queue growth while the framebuffer is intermittently frozen.
implementation: Removed every timer self-IPI latch and flush; trapped WFI and WFE before the hypervisor-wide lock; synchronized virtual IRQ state before and after the real EL2 wait.
verification: RED WFx and source-contract tests failed first; focused suites and complete nested tests passed; complete public suite passed 258/258; clean freestanding build and strict manifest preflight passed.
hardware_result: EXP049 eliminated all excess timer self-IPIs so physical IPI counts exactly matched ordinary SGI queues, but the framebuffer stayed black for more than 90 seconds and TCP/22 never appeared; Stage1 recovered.
notes: The self-IPI storm is fixed and must not return; classify SGI wake coalescing and virtual IRQ Active/deactivation before another delivery-policy change.

title: Stream guest progress without proxy polling
description: Publishes the existing 176-byte EL2 diagnostic sample as a nonblocking asynchronous proxy event every five seconds and records it in the sole assisted launcher.
reason: The old diagnostic snapshot required a host rendezvous request that temporarily woke Windows and changed the failure being measured.
problem_fixed: A spontaneous global pause could not be classified as NVMe, xHCI, timer, vGIC or framebuffer backpressure without perturbing it.
reproduction: Reproduce an EXP050 desktop freeze and observe that the web guest-diagnostic field remains empty until a SIGINT snapshot changes guest progress.
implementation: Added EVT_TELEMETRY=4, exact-sample publication from hv_diag_tick, nonblocking target emission, host accept_event recording and web streaming state; the callback issues zero proxy commands.
verification: RED C and Python contracts failed first; complete public Python suite passed 261/261; complete nested C host suite and focused telemetry/display suites passed; clean Docker build and strict manifest verification passed.
hardware_result: Pending EXP051 hardware validation; no stability verdict is claimed by this observability-only change.
notes: Single changed variable: asynchronous observability transport. WFI/WFE, timers, vGIC, NVMe, xHCI, Mu, topology and memory layout are unchanged.

title: Establish the validated J313 four-efficiency-core baseline
description: Expose only GICC UIDs 0 through 3 to Windows while keeping Firestorm entries disabled and run the current paired m1n1 and Mu artifacts with physical display low memory and runtime diagnostics off.
reason: Repeated mixed E/P runs produced watchdog bugchecks global pauses and slow boot while a fresh Windows installation needed a reproducible control.
problem_fixed: Removes unvalidated Firestorm guest scheduling from the public baseline and prevents diagnostic USB framebuffer traffic from perturbing the first Windows boot.
reproduction: Boot the paired artifacts from Running proxy with physical display debug off and low memory then complete Windows OOBE.
implementation: Disabled MADT GICC flags for UIDs 4 through 7 without changing their topology metadata; retained the proportional NVMe INTx correction and existing four-core timer/vGIC path.
verification: Public root suite passed 265/265; focused m1n1 contract suite passed; exact hashes and launch command are recorded in documentation/STABLE_4E_BASELINE.md.
hardware_result: Fresh Windows ARM64 completed OOBE and reached a responsive desktop; the operator reported normal speed stability and no micro-freezes during the initial session.
notes: Initial hardware baseline only; long-duration stress suspend and Firestorm enablement remain unvalidated. Paired m1n1 SHA-256 is 0389bc92d88f1a19049cecc564b929502f7dbce2ab05942a7e6421bef24632c9.

title: Preserve generated Apple input ACPI device
